description: The same request form in edit mode, reachable only while a request is a draft or has been returned by IDO. It is the requestor's second chance: fix what the reviewer asked for and resubmit under the same document number.

happy_path.action: presses Edit Request on the detail page
happy_path.result: the form loads with every saved value in place and the attachments listed

happy_path.action: changes fields, adds or removes attachments
happy_path.result: removals take effect on save; additions are parked until save
saveDraft runs and the browser returns to /requests/$requestId
saveDraft then submit, in that order, so the resubmission carries the edits — the document number is unchanged

alternate_paths.name: Status changed while the page was open
alternate_paths.trigger: IDO acted on the request in another tab
alternate_paths.result: saveDraft returns FORBIDDEN with the status message; the page shows it and offers a reload rather than losing the typing silently

alternate_paths.name: Not the owner
alternate_paths.trigger: a USER edits an id that is not theirs
alternate_paths.result: FORBIDDEN from saveDraft; the route also refuses because getById already refused

alternate_paths.name: A staff role opens the edit URL
alternate_paths.result: the route gate sends them to /unauthorized — staff never edit a requestor's words

alternate_paths.name: Returned request resubmitted
alternate_paths.result: masterStatus SUBMITTED, a fresh SUBMITTED audit log, the SAME document number, and idoEvaluationStatus is cleared so the request re-enters the IDO queue

trpc_procedures.name: submit
trpc_procedures.description: Defined in spec 005. When resubmitting a RETURNED request it must also clear idoEvaluationStatus, or the request lands back in the queue still flagged as returned.

fields.name: (identical to spec 005)
fields.note: The field set, labels, placeholders and Zod rules are the same object. This spec does not restate them; changing one changes both pages.

functional: The page is reachable only for DRAFT and RETURNED. Any other status renders a read-only notice with a link back to the detail page rather than an editable form the server will refuse.
Form values come from RHF's `values` option, not from a useEffect reset, so a late-resolving query cannot fight the user's typing.
Save Draft returns to /requests/$requestId, the view page — the same rule as spec 005.
Submit performs saveDraft first, so a resubmission always carries the current edits.
Resubmitting a RETURNED request clears idoEvaluationStatus so the IDO queue shows it as a fresh submission rather than as still-returned.
The document number is untouched by any edit or resubmission.
Removing an attachment removes it from the record on save; the S3 object itself is left to s3:sweep, never deleted inline.
The reviewer's return note stays visible while the form is being corrected.
authorization: Server gate: saveDraft and submit both check ownership against the session and both check the status. The route gate stops the wrong role; the procedures stop the wrong request and the wrong moment.
A staff role must not be able to edit request content at all — their influence on the record is finalTitle, reference and notes, through their own review procedures.
The status check is what stops a requestor rewriting a request that is already with the Director.
ux: Navigating away with unsaved changes warns first; a request that took ten minutes to write must not vanish to a stray back button.
Both buttons are disabled while either mutation is in flight and show their pending label.
A FORBIDDEN from a status change while the page was open is shown as a banner naming the new status, with a reload action — not as a bare toast.
Attachment removals are visible immediately in the list but only committed on save, matching the deferred-upload model in the other direction.

rules.zod_rule: saveDraftRequestSchema = createRequestSchema.extend({ id: z.string().min(1) }) — see spec 005 for the field rules

server_guards.error: FORBIDDEN — Request cannot be edited in its current status

server_guards.guard: ownership, SUBMIT_REQUEST and an editable status
documentNumber is reused when already set

covers: resubmitting a RETURNED request keeps its document number
resubmitting writes a second SUBMITTED audit log rather than overwriting the first
editing a request under Director review is FORBIDDEN
editing another user's draft is FORBIDDEN
Edit Request is offered on a draft and not on a submitted request
the reviewer's return note is visible while editing a returned request
Save Draft returns to the detail page
Submit from the edit page carries the edits into the resubmission
navigating away with unsaved changes warns first
a DIRECTOR deep-linking to the edit URL lands on /unauthorized

acceptance_criteria.given: a DRAFT owned by the viewer
acceptance_criteria.then: every saved value is in its field and the attachments are listed

acceptance_criteria.given: a RETURNED request with the note 'Attach the floor plan'
acceptance_criteria.then: the note is pinned above the form

acceptance_criteria.given: an edited RETURNED request with document number 2026-0007
acceptance_criteria.then: the edits are saved first, the status becomes SUBMITTED, and the number is still 2026-0007

acceptance_criteria.given: a request that IDO recommended while the edit page was open
acceptance_criteria.then: the save fails with the status message and the typed values are still on screen

edge_cases: Submit is two mutations. If saveDraft succeeds and submit fails, the edits are already stored — the retry must not re-save, and the user must be told the save landed but the submission did not.
Clearing idoEvaluationStatus on resubmission is easy to forget and produces a request that shows as 'Returned' inside the IDO queue while actually being a new submission.
RHF `values` replaces the whole form when the query object identity changes; make sure the query is not refetching on window focus while the user types, or their edits are overwritten.
An attachment removed but not saved must reappear after a cancel — the removal lives in form state, not in the record.
The status check and the ownership check must both run before the update, and the update must be a single Prisma call on the checked id, or a status change between check and write slips through.
out_of_scope: Any staff-side edit of the record — specs 010-014 own finalTitle, reference and notes.
Version history of edits — AuditLog records lifecycle events, not field diffs, and nothing asks for a diff.
Withdrawing or deleting a request — the old app had neither.
